scope: Matching fixed FMS2 managed phases on the physical iPhone through the connected Codex desktop MCP tools. Two initial inspection timeouts are retained; inspection succeeded only after an explicit USB reconnect.

setupEvidence.scope: Prerequisite ROM setup; no normal build or corpus-test dependency on sibling checkout

limitations: First attachment failed: two five-second SDK deadlines, no Ethernet entry reported by the user, then an explicit unplug/reconnect exposed Ethernet at 192.168.77.16. This is not a clean cold-attachment pass or a firmware fix.
Router/DNS fields, subnet mask and assignment mode were not reported; no routing/lease/Internet coexistence qualification is inferred.
Command-2 exact binary echo and manual D13 lit/off observations are separate from startup; the initialized-data/BSS/counter probe is not migrated or claimed.
The app restart followed an accepted commit reply; this does not qualify actual lost-commit-reply recovery.
No flash-write power loss, SDK ROM programming/recovery, rollback, arbitrary sketch, Pico, minimum-OS or UI/accessibility qualification; no remote CI result claimed.
notes: The matching matrix retains 27 passes, an expected refused restored commit and an expected bootChanged unknown. Four preceding inspection/console reports add two actual attachment failures and two post-reconnect passes.
Exactly two commit phases were accepted, State B then State A. The restored-context commit request was refused without live SDK authority; no commit was replayed.
The first observation script accessed a missing snapshot after exporting the failed inspection. Failed-result handling was corrected; original reports and both timeout attempts remain without replay.

independentCapsuleChecks.description: Actual iPhone default SDK/WASM exports independently accepted by the native firmware FMS2 validator; native checking does not execute ARM code.

attachmentIncident.EthernetAfterExplicitReconnect: visible at 192.168.77.16, as reported by user

validationScopeNote: A local refusal without a checkpoint binds only its explicit operation/record selection, not device observations. Its device context is established by the archived original submission and device-bound stage/restore/reconciliation reports. The offline checker now rejects invented outcome, record-hash or artifact claims on checkpoint-free reports.

offlineValidation.checkerHardening: Checkpoint-free managed nonpasses must remain not_observed and contain no issued-record hash or artifact; they supply no device observation.
